court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: III Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Chennai, O.P.Nos.618 of 2015 & 2274 of 2016
facts_of_case: The parties got married in 2013. The husband filed for divorce citing non-consummation due to impotency. The wife filed for restitution of conjugal rights. The trial court dismissed the divorce petition and allowed the wife's petition.

legal_principles.principle: Parties can settle their disputes and seek a decree by mutual consent.
legal_principles.held: Both the appellant and respondent mutually agree and prayed for dissolution of marriage conducted between them on 20.11.2013.

legal_principles.principle: A Joint Memo of Compromise can be used to settle disputes and seek a decree.
legal_principles.held: The said Joint Memo of Compromise dated 11.08.2022, duly signed by both the appellant as well as respondent and their respective counsel is taken on file and the same is recorded.

outcome.final_order: The marriage was dissolved by mutual consent.

use_for_drafting: drafting divorce petition under Hindu Marriage Act
advising on restitution of conjugal rights
